title: Who is who in The Enemy
back: Dr Sadao (doctor vs patriot), Hana (quiet courage), Tom the prisoner, the self-centred General, the servants (prejudice).

title: The Enemy in six beats
back: Beach → servants refuse → operation → General's promise → escape → why could I not kill him.

back: He removes the bullet, tells the terrified boy not to be afraid, writes a letter to the police — and keeps it in a drawer. The delay measures his conflict.

title: Why could I not kill him?
svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 320 200" role="img" aria-label="Humanity acted before nationalism could" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" font-size="11"><g><circle cx="160" cy="78.2" r="13.2" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.9" stroke="none"/><path d="M142.0,99.4 Q160,91.4 178.0,99.4 L175.12,134.6 L167.2,134.6 L168.64,185 H161.8 L160.72,137.0 H159.28 L158.2,185 H151.36 L152.8,134.6 L144.88,134.6 Z" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.9" stroke="none"/></g><rect x="60" y="30" width="200" height="60" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.08" stroke="none" rx="8"/><text x="160" y="56" text-anchor="middle" font-size="36" font-weight="700" fill="#E0B400" stroke="none">?</text><text x="160.0" y="192" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-style="italic" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.85" stroke="none">Humanity acted before nationalism could</text></svg>
back: At the window he recalls America's prejudice and his dislike of white faces — and still has no answer. Buck's point: the doctor's duty is deeper than the citizen's.

title: The title's question
svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 320 200" role="img" aria-label="Line to remember" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" font-size="11"><g><rect x="28" y="36" width="264" height="72" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.08" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" rx="10"/><path d="M50,108 L42,122 L64,108 Z" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.9" stroke="none"/><text x="160.0" y="79.7" text-anchor="middle" font-size="22" font-weight="700" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">The Enemy</text></g><text x="160" y="146" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.8" stroke="none">— who is the enemy: the prisoner, the war, or prejudice?</text><text x="160.0" y="192" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-style="italic" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.85" stroke="none">Line to remember</text></svg>
back: The man his country calls the enemy becomes a patient and a human being; prejudice on both sides is the real enemy.
